title: Instruction Tuning: Same Loss, a Different Task

images.caption: Stanford's Alpaca (2023): an AI teacher wrote 52,000 instruction-response examples, and LLaMA 7B became an instruction-following model. Numbers as published by the Stanford team.
images.target_after_text: OpenAI's text-davinci-003 generated the examples, for less than $500. Training took 3 hours on 8 GPUs, for less than $1...
images.target_after_text_full: OpenAI's text-davinci-003 generated the examples, for less than $500. Training took 3 hours on 8 GPUs, for less than $100. In a small blind comparison run by the team, Alpaca and text-davinci-003 were preferred almost equally often: 90 to 89.
images.next_text: Alpaca also gave wrong answers. Asked for the capital of Tanzania, it answered Dar es Salaam. The capital is Dodoma.
images.next_text_full: Alpaca also gave wrong answers. Asked for the capital of Tanzania, it answered Dar es Salaam. The capital is Dodoma.

images.caption: LIMA (2023): 1,000 curated examples and no RL on top of LLaMA 65B; 43% of answers rated equal to or better than GPT-4's. Published result.
images.target_after_text: LIMA (2023) fine-tuned a 65B LLaMA model on only 1,000 curated examples, with no reinforcement learning. In the authors...
images.target_after_text_full: LIMA (2023) fine-tuned a 65B LLaMA model on only 1,000 curated examples, with no reinforcement learning. In the authors' human evaluation, 43% of its answers were rated equal to or better than GPT-4's. The authors conclude that almost all of a model's knowledge comes from pretraining, and that a small amount of instruction data mainly determines how it answers.
images.next_text: FLAN (2021) rewrote more than 60 NLP tasks as natural-language instructions and fine-tuned a 137B model on them. On tas...
images.next_text_full: FLAN (2021) rewrote more than 60 NLP tasks as natural-language instructions and fine-tuned a 137B model on them. On tasks absent from training, it outperformed the 175B GPT-3 in the zero-shot setting on 20 of 25 tests.
images.target_block_html: LIMA (2023) fine-tuned a 65B LLaMA model on only 1,000 curated examples, with no reinforcement learning. In the authors' human evaluation, 43% of its answers were rated equal to or better than GPT-4's. The authors conclude that almost all of a model's knowledge comes from pretraining, and that a small amount of instruction data mainly determines how it answers.

images.caption: FLAN (2021): a 137B model tuned on 60+ tasks phrased as instructions beat zero-shot GPT-3 175B on 20 of 25 unseen tasks. Published result; which tiles stay grey is illustrative.
images.target_after_text: FLAN (2021) rewrote more than 60 NLP tasks as natural-language instructions and fine-tuned a 137B model on them. On tas...
images.target_after_text_full: FLAN (2021) rewrote more than 60 NLP tasks as natural-language instructions and fine-tuned a 137B model on them. On tasks absent from training, it outperformed the 175B GPT-3 in the zero-shot setting on 20 of 25 tests.
images.next_text: Instruction tuning therefore teaches a general ability to follow instructions, which transfers to tasks not seen in tra...
images.next_text_full: Instruction tuning therefore teaches a general ability to follow instructions, which transfers to tasks not seen in training. That is why it is the first step of post-training: the model first learns to answer instructions, and preference alignment and reinforcement learning then improve the quality of those answers.
images.target_block_html: FLAN (2021) rewrote more than 60 NLP tasks as natural-language instructions and fine-tuned a 137B model on them. On tasks absent from training, it outperformed the 175B GPT-3 in the zero-shot setting on 20 of 25 tests.

images.caption: The prompt gets no loss, but the response's gradient still flows back to it through attention. Schematic.
images.target_after_text: The loss mask decides which predictions count toward the loss. It doesn't change which tokens attention reads. The resp...
images.target_after_text_full: The loss mask decides which predictions count toward the loss. It doesn't change which tokens attention reads. The response depends on reading the prompt, so the gradient from the response's loss flows back through attention to the prompt tokens and updates the parameters that process them.

images.caption: The loss is averaged over loss tokens, so a 500-token response weighs 250 times as much as a 2-token one. Illustrative counts.
images.target_after_text: Length matters when mixing data. The loss is averaged over loss tokens, so longer responses take a larger share: a 500-...
images.target_after_text_full: Length matters when mixing data. The loss is averaged over loss tokens, so longer responses take a larger share: a 500-token response weighs about 250 times as much as a 2-token response. A mix should therefore be balanced by token count, not only by number of examples.
